info.name: Discord Daily Attendance & Update Automation API
info.description:
API collection for the Discord Daily Attendance & Update Automation backend.

## Authentication Model
- **Admin Only**: System login and dashboard access is permitted exclusively for administrators.
- **Direct Attendance**: Regular users/students do not log in or register; they submit daily attendance directly via the public web attendance form.

## Auto Token Management
The Admin Login request automatically saves the access token as a collection variable. All authenticated requests use it via the collection-level pre-request script.

request.description:
Requires admin auth. Starts a full guild member re-sync and returns immediately with 202 Accepted; the sync itself runs in the background. Returns 409 if a sync is already running, or 503 if the bot is not connected.

**Multi-server.** Body is `{ guildId?: string }`; sync every configured server when omitted, or narrow to a single ID. Response is a fan-out envelope with `data.guildIds[]` (the targeted servers) plus `data.servers[]` (per-server outcomes); partial success is HTTP 202 — read `data.servers[]`, a `success: true` does NOT mean every server worked. Only a total failure returns an error status.

item.name: Channel Schedule
item.description:
Admin-managed open/lock schedule for #daily-update (requires ADMIN role).

The times are stored in the database, not in code or .env, and take effect without a restart. Times are HH:mm wall-clock in Asia/Dhaka; the cron expression is derived by the backend and never exposed.

Operational prerequisite: the bot needs "Manage Roles" on the channel to edit the @everyone SendMessages overwrite. Without it every open and lock fails and `scheduler.lastRun.error` says so.

request.description:
Requires admin auth. Returns four things:

- `schedule` - the stored openTime, closeTime, daysOfWeek (0=Sunday..6=Saturday), enabled flag, the fixed `timezone` (Asia/Dhaka, reported but never accepted), and who last changed it.
- `scheduler` - whether THIS process runs the timed jobs (`processEnabled`, from SCHEDULER_ENABLED), whether jobs are registered (`running`), `nextOpenAt` / `nextLockAt` as instants, and `lastRun`.
- `channel` - the configured channel ID and its LIVE open state, read from Discord rather than a stored flag.

Check `scheduler.lastRun.error` first when the channel stops opening: a missing Manage Roles permission surfaces here and nowhere else.

item.name: Roster
item.description:
The enrolment roster and the switch that arms the attendance email check. Every route requires ADMIN auth without exception - this holds the names, email addresses and phone numbers of every enrolled student, and there is no membership check that could stand in for a credential here.

How the feature is turned on, in order:
1. POST /roster/import - upload the spreadsheet.
2. GET /roster and GET /roster/settings - check the roll looks right (settings reports `activeEntries`).
3. PATCH /roster/settings { enforceEmail: true } - arm it. Takes effect on the next submission, no restart.

Rollback is PATCH /roster/settings { enforceEmail: false }: one request, immediate, no deploy.

Two properties worth knowing before you touch it. An import UPSERTS by normalized email and can never deactivate anybody, so a truncated or wrong file adds noise rather than locking students out. And enabling enforcement is REFUSED while the roster has no active entries, because arming an empty gate refuses every student in every server with a correct-looking 403 and no error anywhere.

request.description:
Requires admin auth. Multipart upload, field name `file`. Accepts .xlsx and .csv.

In Postman: Body > form-data > key `file`, type File, then pick the spreadsheet.

Columns are located by HEADER NAME, never by position, matched case-insensitively after trimming:
- email: email, email address, e-mail, e mail, mail
- name: name, full name, student name, fullname
- phone: phone, phone number, mobile, mobile number, contact, contact number

Unrecognized columns (batch, roll number, ...) are ignored. A sheet with no email or no name column is a 400 naming the headers found, with NOTHING written - every row would fail identically, so a summary of 5,000 identical failures would be a worse report.

A legacy binary .xls is a 400 telling you to re-save as .xlsx (the parser genuinely cannot read that format).

Partial success is a 200, not an error. Valid rows load; invalid ones are skipped and listed in `data.rejectedRows` with the sheet's own row numbers and a reason. An error status would say nothing happened and invite a re-upload, when those rows really did load.

An address repeated inside one sheet resolves to ONE entry - the last row wins - and is reported in `data.duplicateAddresses` with every row number involved.

request.description:
Requires admin auth. Reports of attendance submissions whose submitted handle did not match the recorded Discord pairing for the same email. One row per open report (or per the status filter), joined to the enrolled entry and the paired / submitting account handles.

Reports are produced when a paired student submits attendance with a different handle AND ticks the `cannotEnterRealDiscordUsername` flag on the attendance form. The first write of the day is recorded; subsequent mismatched submissions on the same day are absorbed by the partial unique index and do not create duplicate rows.

The listing deliberately rejects `pairedAccountId` and `submittingAccountId` filters (400) — combining them would let a caller enumerate Discord account snowflakes. Filter by status, search, and date range only.

Ordering is `reportedAt DESC` so the dashboard's first page is the most recent activity.

item.name: Act on Discord Pairing Mismatch Report

request.description:
Requires admin auth. Closes an open mismatch report.

`action` is `reassign` or `dismiss`. Anything else is a 400.

REASSIGN rewrites the entry's pairing to the submitted account, but only if the entry still holds the original paired account — a single conditional write that preserves the invariant against a stale dashboard. The membership check runs first: reassigning to a Discord account that has left every configured server is refused with 422, because the entry would end up paired to nothing. The report and the pairing rewrite are in one transaction; either both happen or neither does.

DISMISS closes the report and leaves the pairing untouched. No membership check; the recorded pairing is the administrator's decision that the existing record is correct.

Either action on a closed report is refused with 409 and the current status. An unknown id is 404. The action writes an audit-log entry with the action, the report id, the reviewing admin, and the time.

item.name: Reminders
item.description:
Rate-limited reminder DM broadcasts (BullMQ + Redis).

Every route requires admin auth. POST /send DMs thousands of students and CANNOT be undone, so the intended flow is: GET /targets to confirm the count, then POST /send, then poll GET /:id for progress.

Delivery is paced at REMINDER_DM_PER_SECOND (default 2), so a 5,000-member broadcast takes ~40 minutes. That is Golden Rule 4, not a performance bug.

request.description:
Who WOULD be reminded for a Dhaka date: members currently in the guild with no daily update that day. Sends nothing.

`date` is required and never inferred - an inferred date near midnight would remind the wrong day's members with nothing looking wrong. A future date is rejected.

Range mode: replace `date` with `from`+`to` (max 92 days), optional `daysOfWeek` and `criterion` (default `MISSING_UPDATE`), `minMissedDays` (default 1). See "Get Reminder Targets - Missed 2 of the Past 3 Days" below for the worked example.

Starts a broadcast. Answers 202 - NOTHING has been delivered when this returns; delivery runs in the background at the configured rate.

Guards, in order: Redis must be reachable (503), no other broadcast overlapping the requested period may be running (409), and the target list must be non-empty (400). Recipient rows are written BEFORE any job is enqueued, so a crash leaves a visibly incomplete run rather than one that looks finished.

Save the returned `id` - it is how you read progress and cancel.

Body is `{ date?, from?, to?, daysOfWeek?, criterion?, minMissedDays?, message, guildIds? }`. `date` is the single-date mode (unchanged); replace with `from`+`to` for range mode (max 92 days). `criterion` defaults to `MISSING_UPDATE` so an existing single-date send is unchanged. `minMissedDays` defaults to 1. See "Send Reminder Broadcast - Date Range" for the range example.

**Multi-server.** Covers every configured server unless `guildIds` narrows it. One Discord account receives exactly ONE DM even when targeted through several servers — `targetCount` counts recipient rows, `uniqueRecipients` counts people. The overlap 409 stays global, because it guards the bot's single shared DM budget.

exec: // Keep the id for the progress, recipients and cancel requests.

request.description:
Live progress for one broadcast. This is what Phase 7's SSE endpoint will stream.

The counts are read from the recipient rows, which are the source of truth - not from the cached counters on the session row. `outstanding` is how many are still unattempted.

Per-recipient delivery outcomes - the audit view. Add `status=DELIVERED` | `DM_CLOSED` | `FAILED` | `PENDING` to filter.

PENDING after a broadcast ended means never attempted (for example after a cancel), NOT failed. Contact details are deliberately not exposed here.
Broadcast history, newest first, with the admin who started each run. The originating admin may be null if that account was later deleted - the audit trail outlives it.

Stops a broadcast in flight - the stop button for a message sent with a typo.

The status write IS the cancel: the worker re-reads it before every send, so queued and in-flight jobs stop delivering even though jobs already started cannot be removed from Redis. Already-delivered recipients keep their outcome; the rest stay PENDING because they were never attempted. Cancelling a finished broadcast is a 409.

Queue and worker health.

Check `lastFallback` first when members with closed DMs say they were never told: a missing "Send Messages" permission on #daily-update-reminder delivers every DM successfully and silently reaches nobody who needed the fallback. It surfaces here and nowhere else.

`workerRunning` is false when the Discord bot never connected - a job cannot DM without a gateway connection, so the worker waits for it.

item.name: Get Reminder Targets - Missed 2 of the Past 3 Days

request.description:
The worked example. A three-day range with criterion MISSING_BOTH and minMissedDays 2 targets exactly the accounts that submitted NEITHER attendance NOR a daily update on at least two of the three counted days.

`criterion` defaults to MISSING_UPDATE - what a broadcast meant before ranges existed - so an existing single-date send is unchanged. MISSING_BOTH is opt-in.

Creates nothing and sends nothing. The same set is visible at GET /daily-status?from=...&to=...&minMissedBothDays=2, because both derive from one shared query.

item.name: Get Reminder Targets - Threshold Exceeds Span (400)

request.description: A minMissedDays higher than the number of counted days can never be met, so it is refused rather than run as a broadcast that always finds nobody.

Sends to everyone who missed BOTH submissions on at least 2 of the 3 counted days.

The period, criterion, threshold and weekday set are all persisted on the run: recomputing 'who would this have targeted' from current data gives a different answer as members join and leave, so the rule is recorded rather than inferred.

A single-date send stores the same date at both ends. `reminderDate` no longer exists on any reminder payload - read `reminderStartDate` and `reminderEndDate`.

  "from": "2026-08-15",

  "criterion": "MISSING_BOTH",
  "minMissedDays": 2,
  "message": "You have missed both attendance and your daily update on two or more of the last three days. Please catch up today."
}

item.name: Attendance Announcement
item.description:
The evening announcement posted to #attendance (requires ADMIN role). Nothing here is student-facing.

The message and its schedule are stored in the database, not in code or .env, and take effect without a restart. announceTime is HH:mm wall-clock in Asia/Dhaka; the cron expression is derived by the backend and never exposed.

⚠️ MENTIONS: they come ONLY from the structured allowlist (mentionRoleIds, mentionUsernames, mentionEveryone). Mention text typed into the body is inert — allowedMentions is built from the allowlist alone, so a stray @everyone in the message cannot ping anybody. Conversely, mentionEveryone: true pings every member of the guild every evening until it is turned off.

DUPLICATES: at most one post per Dhaka day, enforced by a database claim rather than by timing. A second send returns 409; { "force": true } is the only way past it. Beneath that, every send carries enforceNonce with a deterministic nonce, because discord.js retries a REST call that times out and Discord may already have created the message — without the nonce one logical send can leave several identical messages in the channel.

Operational prerequisite: the bot needs "Send Messages" on the attendance channel. Without it every send fails, which is reported as a 403 on send and under `scheduler.lastOutcome` on the read.

request.description:
Requires admin auth. Returns:

- `template` - the stored body with placeholders unexpanded, terminationDays, the mention allowlist, the @everyone flag, and who last changed it.
- `schedule` - announceTime, daysOfWeek (0=Sunday..6=Saturday), enabled, and the fixed `timezone` (Asia/Dhaka, reported but never accepted).
- `preview` - the message exactly as it would be posted right now: placeholders expanded, mention line appended, its length against Discord's 2000-character limit, the closeTime it read from the #daily-update schedule, and which allowlist entries resolved.
- `supportedPlaceholders` - the only tokens a body may use.
- `scheduler` - whether THIS process runs the timed post (`processEnabled`, from SCHEDULER_ENABLED), whether a task is registered (`running`), `nextRunAt`, and `lastOutcome`.
- `today` - whether today has been posted, and every attempt with its status and error.

Check `scheduler.lastOutcome` first when the channel goes quiet: a missing Send Messages permission surfaces here.

item.name: Daily Status
item.description:
Admin dashboard daily status aggregation and export endpoints (requires ADMIN role).

Provides overview status counts for a date, paginated active member status table with filtering and search, single member daily update message audit, and streamed CSV export.

query.description: Asia/Dhaka civil date (YYYY-MM-DD)
Optional. Narrow to one configured server; omit for every server. An unconfigured ID is a 400.

request.description:
Summary overview figures for a given date. Guaranteed JSON numbers.

Invariant: `bothComplete + missingUpdateOnly + missingAttendanceOnly + missingBoth === totalMembers`.

The combined figures count PEOPLE - a Discord account in two configured servers counts once. `byServer` counts each server's own memberships, so the same account counts once in each.

IMPORTANT: `byServer` deliberately does NOT sum to the combined totals. The difference between them is exactly the number of people who are in more than one server. Do not treat it as a total and its parts.

Optional `guildId` narrows WHO is counted; it never changes anyone's status, because a daily update posted in any server credits the account everywhere.

query.description: Asia/Dhaka civil date (YYYY-MM-DD)
Optional. Narrow to one configured server; omit for every server. An unconfigured ID is a 400.

request.description:
Paginated status table for a date - ONE ROW PER PERSON, not per server membership.

A student in two servers appears once. Their row carries `servers` (every server they are in, narrowed by `guildId` when supplied), `serverCount` (the true total, never narrowed - so `servers.length` of 1 with `serverCount` of 2 means 'also in another server'), `memberId` (the representative record, safe to use for /members/:memberId) and `memberIds` (all of them).

Status credits work done in ANY server: an update posted in server A makes the account COMPLETE in server B too. Do not merge or split rows client-side - the row is already the person.

item.name: Get Daily Status Page - Filtered by Status

query.description: COMPLETE | MISSING_UPDATE | MISSING_ATTENDANCE | MISSING_BOTH
Optional. Narrow to one configured server; omit for every server. An unconfigured ID is a 400.

request.description: Filtered by status. Meta total reflects the filtered count of PEOPLE, not memberships.

query.description: Case-insensitive partial match on name, phone, email, or discordUsername
Optional. Narrow to one configured server; omit for every server. An unconfigured ID is a 400.

request.description:
Searches member directory fields case-insensitively.

Matching is per person: a term that matches an account's nickname in only one of its servers still returns that account once, with every one of its servers intact.

One PERSON's status and their posted #daily-update messages for that date. 404 if memberId is unknown.

The memberId identifies a member record, but the response describes the whole Discord account behind it: either server's record returns the same answer. The response carries `servers` (every server the account is in), `serverCount` (the true total, never narrowed by filters), and `memberIds` (every member record, aligned with `servers`). `messages` merges every server's messages into one timeline ordered by send time, each carrying `guildId` and `serverLabel`.

Range mode: replace `date` with `from`+`to` (max 92 days), optional `daysOfWeek`. Range mode adds a `days` array (one entry per counted day with that day's status, hasAttendance, hasDailyUpdate) in place of the single-date status fields, plus the per-day counts.

query.description: Optional. Narrow to one configured server; omit for every server. An unconfigured ID is a 400.

request.description:
Streams filtered daily status rows as a CSV file attachment - one row per PERSON. Values with =, +, -, @ are escaped to prevent formula injection.

The leading `servers` column lists every server the person belongs to, pipe-separated.

`format=xlsx` returns 501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED in both date and range modes (the same response the roster engagement export uses); use `format=csv` (the default).

Range mode replaces `date` with `from`+`to` (max 92 days), optional `daysOfWeek`, `rangeStatus` and `minMissedBothDays` filters. The header row names the range count columns and the filename identifies the span.

item.name: Get Daily Status Counts - Date Range

request.description:
Range-wide overview. Returns totalMembers plus the three rollup buckets (allCompleteMembers/partialMembers/noneMembers, which sum to it) and the person-day totals attendanceDays/updateDays/completeDays/missedBothDays.

The person-day totals are named DIFFERENTLY from the seven single-date figures on purpose - they count person-days, not people. `byServer` still does not sum to the combined totals; the gap is the overlap.

`daysOfWeek` (0=Sunday) picks which weekdays count; omit it to count every day. The response echoes it plus the resulting `daysInRange`, so the figure always travels with its denominator.

item.name: Get Daily Status Page - Date Range

request.description:
One row per PERSON, with per-day counts replacing the single-day status.

WATCH OUT: `incompleteDays` and `missedBothDays` are DIFFERENT figures. Someone who submits attendance every day and never posts an update has incompleteDays = daysInRange and missedBothDays = 0. The reminder threshold acts on missedBothDays. There is deliberately no field called `missedDays`.

Range-only sorts: missedBothDays, completeDays, rangeStatus.

item.name: Get Daily Status Page - Range Filtered by Rollup

request.description: `rangeStatus` (ALL_COMPLETE | PARTIAL | NONE) replaces `status` in range mode. Passing the single-date `status` filter with a range is a 400 rather than a filter that is accepted and silently does nothing.

item.name: Get Daily Status Page - Preview a Reminder Target Set

request.description: Filters on the SAME computed column the reminder thresholds on, so this lists exactly who a MISSING_BOTH broadcast at minMissedDays=2 would contact - in the list an admin already knows how to read, before opening the send dialog.

item.name: Get Daily Status Page - Reversed Range (400)

request.description:
Each range mistake is its own 400 naming the specific conflict:
- to earlier than from (this request)
- a span over 92 days
- `date` together with `from`/`to`
- a lone `from` or `to`
- `daysOfWeek` with a single `date`
- `daysOfWeek` leaving no counted day
- `status` with a range, or `rangeStatus`/`minMissedBothDays` with a date

item.name: Get Member Daily Status - Date Range

request.description: The account's range counts, a `days` array with one entry per counted day (hasAttendance, hasDailyUpdate and that day's four-bucket status), and the merged message timeline for the range across every server. Weekdays excluded by `daysOfWeek` are absent from `days`.

item.name: Export Daily Status CSV - Date Range

request.description: Range export: the header row names the range count columns and rangeStatus, and the filename identifies the span. The single-date export header is unchanged.
